title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short handwritten note in Grothendieck's hand. It is written over a faint typed text, apparently a reused Bourbaki-style draft (the neighbouring 'pages' are such typed drafts and are unrelated). It refers to a 'formule précédente' not on this page. That formula was probably the comparison, for a compact complex manifold or smooth projective variety (or a point/curve case), between the topological trace/integration and the analytic (Serre–Grothendieck duality, residue-normalized) trace, with a factor (2πi)^{-n}.

The note generalizes this to any proper morphism f: X → Y of complex manifolds ('variétés holomorphes'; 'algébriques' is crossed out) of constant relative dimension p. Grothendieck writes 'codimension relative p', but the degree drop of 2p forces fibre dimension p.

The boxed square is:
- top row: H^i(X,C) → H^{i-2p}(Y,C), via f_*^top, the topological Gysin map or integration along the fibres;
- verticals: the holomorphic de Rham isomorphisms H^i(X,C) ≅ H^i(X,Ω^•_X) (hypercohomology);
- bottom row: (2πi)^{-p} f_*^an, where f_*^an is the trace morphism Rf_*Ω^•_X[2p] → Ω^•_Y coming from analytic Grothendieck–Verdier duality, normalized by residues.

The claim is that the square commutes. The factor arises because the residue-normalized trace gives Res(dz/z) = 1, whereas the topological integral of the corresponding class is ∮dz/z = 2πi. The note ends: hence an analogous generalization for algebraic varieties over C. That would follow via GAGA, with algebraic de Rham cohomology and the algebraic trace of coherent duality.

In the context of 'Motifs et théorie de Hodge', the purpose is to fix the normalization of Gysin/trace maps between Betti and de Rham realizations. The factor (2πi)^p is exactly the Tate-twist discrepancy Q(-p) between the Betti and de Rham lattices.
errors: 'codimension relative p' should be relative dimension p (fibre dimension p), given that the map lowers degree by 2p. Alternatively, codimension must be read as −p.

The constant depends on conventions. With C^∞ de Rham forms and fibre integration no factor appears. The (2πi)^{-p} is correct for the residue-normalized coherent trace, but there is a possible sign ((−1)^p, or a sign depending on degree/orientation conventions) that the note does not address.
The bottom map should carry a shift of the Hodge filtration by p (a Tate twist); this is not indicated. It is harmless for the statement over C.

ideas.what: Compatibility of topological Gysin/fibre integration with the analytic Grothendieck duality trace on holomorphic de Rham cohomology, up to (2πi)^{-p}, for proper morphisms of relative dimension p
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of Betti and de Rham trace/Gysin maps; fundamental class and trace compatibility (Tate twist normalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verdier (cohomology classes and trace compatibility), El Zein (1978, complexe dualisant et classe fondamentale), Deligne (Hodge II/III normalizations of 2πi)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas appear in Grothendieck's de Rham cohomology paper (IHES 1966) and in Hartshorne's Residues and Duality; the exact statement is unsure

ideas.what: Transfer of the statement to algebraic varieties over C via GAGA
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham trace and comparison isomorphism compatible with Gysin maps

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief normalization remark: Betti versus coherent-duality traces differ by (2πi)^p. That is standard and well documented in the later literature (Deligne, Verdier, El Zein). It contains nothing unfinished or unknown, only a slip in 'codimension'.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out word before 'holomorphes' appears to be 'algébriques' (struck through), as the machine transcription suggests.

The cohomological degrees in the boxed diagram are hard to read; they look like H^{i} (possibly H^{2i} or a similar superscript) on the left and H^{i-2p} on the right. The bottom row is hypercohomology of Ω^•_X and Ω^•_Y.
The faint typed text in the background is a different document reused as scrap paper (a Bourbaki-style draft), not part of these notes.
The text should be read as 'partout de codimension relative p' (sic), which mathematically means relative dimension p.
